headline: Atlassian and OpenAI have widened their partnership, with OpenAI's newest models to power AI agents across Atlassian's products while Atlassian keeps using several AI models.
score_reason: Facts read through a secondary outlet; the 'spend commitment' in VentureBeat's headline is not in the posts as described.
importance_line: OpenAI gets a larger role inside a widely used workplace tool, which matters to Atlassian's customers, but neither company post gives a price, a term or a dollar figure, according to FourWeekMBA.
summary: Atlassian, maker of the Jira and Confluence work-tracking software, and OpenAI each published posts on 6 Oct 2026 about an expanded deal that builds on a 2023 collaboration; VentureBeat's headline calls it a spend commitment, but FourWeekMBA, which read both posts, says neither gives a price, contract length or dollar value. OpenAI's post says its GPT-6 family will power agents across Atlassian's platform, while Atlassian describes OpenAI's new models as an addition to the mix of models in its Rovo AI assistant, so it is not tied to OpenAI alone.
notes: VentureBeat blocked (429). Source set to AI News Desk: built from VentureBeat's headline, FourWeekMBA's reading of the Atlassian and OpenAI posts, and the Atlassian blog link. The 'spend commitment' appears only in VentureBeat's headline.
